questions.question_text:
What is the area of this L-shaped room in $\text{m}^2$?
Its outside dimensions are $300\text{ cm}$ high and $110\text{ cm}$ wide at the upper section; the lower section extends $2.5\text{ m}$ beyond it and is $1\text{ m}$ high.

options.why: $58$ is ten times the correct area. Convert the centimetre lengths to metres first.
The converted rectangles have areas $3.3\text{ m}^2$ and $2.5\text{ m}^2$, giving $5.8\text{ m}^2$, not $7.6\text{ m}^2$.
The two rectangle areas add to $5.8\text{ m}^2$, not $82.5\text{ m}^2$.

questions.solution_text:
Use metres for all lengths.
$300\text{ cm}=3\text{ m}$ and $110\text{ cm}=1.1\text{ m}$.
The upper-width rectangle covers the full $3\text{ m}$ height.
Its area is $1.1+1.1+1.1=3.3\text{ m}^2$.
The lower extension has area $2.5\times1=2.5\text{ m}^2$.
$3.3+2.5=5.8\text{ m}^2$
